coverage.note: Coverage is a hard condition, not an observation: the builder exits non-zero on a single lost station-year, so an incomplete panel cannot be scored as the frozen one.

extraction_cost.route: daily_max_min features + HTF daily flags, one request each per station-year
extraction_cost.note: The route matters: the raw 6-minute series would have been 29,160 requests and about 15.2 GiB. One request per station-year per product is 4,880 requests and about 184 MB, and it is the publisher's own verified product.

label_route.source: NOAA HTF daily product, field minFlag (the publisher's own minor-flood days)
label_route.correction: our reduction of 6-minute maxima overcounted flood days by ~20% against NOAA's own counts on 2024 (113-114 vs 94 over four stations); NOAA's own flags matched exactly, station by station
label_route.note: A label that disagrees with the publisher's own product has to be justified, and there is no reason to ship one. Our own reduction overcounted by about 20%.

datum.requirement: MUST use datum=STND. The published nos_minor threshold is in the station datum and the metadata API does not declare a datum. Comparing MLLW-referenced heights to nos_minor silently yields zero positives at every station; see measurements.datum_trap_measured.

measured.purpose: Regression fixture for NOAA CO-OPS datum handling. Recorded so a future change cannot silently reintroduce the MLLW-vs-threshold bug, which produced zero positives at every station.
measured.rule: Compare observed water levels to the published NOS flood thresholds using datum=STND. The MDAPI floodlevels response carries no datum field, and datum=MLLW makes the comparison silently fail.

cases.name: bomb-cyclone record tide
cases.why: Boston's documented record tide. Any datum handling that denies flooding here is wrong.

cases.name: 2025 annual maximum
cases.why: The highest tide of the station-year used for the base-rate measurement.

external_validation.claim: NOAA's authoritative annual product reports minCount 2 for 2025, matching the STND reconstruction (2 exceeding days) and contradicting the MLLW one (0).

threshold_decision.decision: the published physical nos_minor threshold is retained
threshold_decision.why: it is the quantity coastal flood statements are actually issued against; it is not replaced with a per-station quantile chosen to balance the classes

baseline.note: The benchmark's own train.py and validate.py, copied verbatim and shipped here. Measured on the corrected artifact, fetched from staging rather than rebuilt: the artifact is already gated, and these are the numbers the release carries. The superseded artifact's pair (0.8638 / 0.8688) is kept in the candidate record.

independent_reproduction.note: the earlier clean-room reproduction ran against the superseded artifact; a new consumer check must run against these bytes before the package claims it

persistence_calibration.command: python3 code/persistence_baseline.py --fetch (eval split only; no training)
persistence_calibration.why: the honest floor: what a single stock feature achieves with no learning at all
persistence_calibration.accuracy_trap: the plain rule 'yesterday exceeded the threshold' agrees with the label about 96% of the time while scoring 0.63 AUC, because only ~2% of days are positive. Accuracy would flatter a useless rule, which is why the contract scores AUC.
